title: Magnetism Check
summary: This lesson explores the fundamental properties of magnets, including their attraction to iron, polar characteristics, magnetic fields, and application in compasses using Earth's magnetic field. Students will examine how opposite poles attract and like poles repel.

sections.text: Scene: A diagram showing a magnet pulling an iron object toward it. Every magnet is illustrated with a north and south pole clearly labeled at opposite ends.
Scene: Two magnets are shown with their poles facing each other. Opposite poles attract while like poles repel, and the magnetic field lines show the greatest concentration of strength at the poles.

key_concepts: Magnetic field is strongest at the poles
learning_objectives: Identify that magnets attract iron and possess north and south poles
Explain how opposite and like poles interact with each other
Describe where the magnetic field is strongest and how compasses function

vocabulary.definition: An object that attracts iron and has a north and south pole
The area around a magnet that is strongest at the poles
A tool that uses Earth's magnetic field to show direction
